name: Interferon beta-1a
route_note: Avonex intramuscular once weekly; Rebif subcutaneous three times weekly; Plegridy SC or IM every two weeks.

discovery.note: The human interferon beta gene was cloned in 1980; beta-1a is the glycosylated form produced in Chinese hamster ovary cells, identical in sequence to natural interferon beta.

tagline: Long-established injectable disease-modifying therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis
summary: Interferon beta-1a is a recombinant glycosylated form of human interferon beta used to reduce relapses in multiple sclerosis. Introduced in the 1990s, it was one of the first disease-modifying MS therapies and has a long safety record.
mechanism: Interferon beta binds the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1/IFNAR2), activating JAK-STAT signalling and expression of hundreds of interferon-stimulated genes.

In multiple sclerosis it is thought to reduce T-cell activation and migration across the blood–brain barrier (partly by lowering matrix metalloproteinase activity and adhesion molecules), shift cytokine production toward anti-inflammatory profiles and decrease antigen presentation.
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, including clinically isolated syndrome

history.title: Interferon discovered
history.detail: Alick Isaacs and Jean Lindenmann describe interferon as a factor that interferes with viral replication.

history.title: Gene cloned
history.detail: The human interferon beta gene is cloned.

history.title: First MS interferon
history.detail: Interferon beta-1b (Betaseron) becomes the first FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy for MS.

history.title: Avonex
history.detail: The FDA approves Biogen's once-weekly intramuscular interferon beta-1a.

history.title: Rebif in Europe
history.detail: Serono's subcutaneous interferon beta-1a is approved in the EU.

history.title: Rebif in the US
history.detail: The FDA approves Rebif after the EVIDENCE head-to-head trial overcame Avonex's orphan exclusivity.

history.title: Plegridy
history.detail: Peginterferon beta-1a, dosed every two weeks, is approved in the EU and US.

pk.half_life: about 10 hours (IM Avonex); longer for peginterferon
pk.bioavailability: absorbed after IM or SC injection; absolute bioavailability not well defined
pk.metabolism: proteolytic catabolism, mainly hepatic and renal

facts: Interferon beta-1a differs from beta-1b, which is made in E. coli, is not glycosylated and has a serine substituted at position 17.
